newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT - Leumi Insurance overprice.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Leumi Insurance overprice.

text.p: Israel's Leumi Insurance Holdings is overpriced, even though Assicurazioni Generali SpA of Italy is due to make a tender offer for the shares this week at a 28 percent premium, Bank Hapoalim said on Monday.

Analyst Benny Sharvit noted that the offer was for up to 42.202 percent of any one shareholder's holding so that a seller would not be able to capture the full value Generali has assigned to the shares.
Generali is offering to buy shares in Leumi Insurance, Israel's biggest insurance company, for 3.3148 shekels each, versus a closing price on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange on Sunday of 2.59 shekels.
The offer values Leumi Insurance as a whole at $1.01 billion, a premium, Sharvit said, Generali was paying for control of the company.
Based on its current market valuation of $793 million, Sharvit estimated the underlying value of Leumi Insurance was $632 million after discounting the effect of the tender offer.

"Because Generali will purchase only about 42 percent of the public's holdings, in our opinion, purchasing Leumi Insurance shares today at the $793 million valuation, selling 42 percent of them to Generali ... and selling the remaining 58 percent in the market at the current market price will not ensure a return for the investor," Sharvit said.
"A transaction of this sort would only be worthwhile if the price of the share fell at least 20 percent to 2.06 shekels," he added.
Hapoalim said those interested in buying Leumi Insurance as a long-term investment should wait until after the offer is completed when the price is expected to fall.
Hapoalim noted that Genrali had acquired a 1.95 percent stake in Leumi Insurance from Bank Leumi at the end of 1996 at a valuation of $650 million, which he added was close to his own estimate.

Generali's tender offer will be based on Leumi Insurance's closing price at the end of trading on Tuesday. The offer aims to increase the Italian insurer's stake in the company to 57.9 percent from its current 27.2 percent.
